_notes: Taito do Brasil, 1981-82 firmware (four 2KB ROMs). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the Vortex ROM and live
NVRAM captures on an AtGames ALP4K (Visual Pinball Standalone); the other sets listed share Vortex's boot code
byte-for-byte and were checked against a saved image each (high score, settings block, display layout).
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The settings block 0x4070-0x4078 is nine BCD bytes edited from the service menu, validated at reset
(a non-BCD byte restores all nine from ROM); only balls-per-game is identified. 0x4074-0x4076 are the three
replay levels, one byte each, whose scale is not confirmed and so are not declared. No checksum.
A game in progress is deliberately resumed by the firmware at reset; PinMAME's taito driver (2026-10) marks
the saved game over on load so a table starts in attract.

player_count._notes: Read by the reset path, which refuses to resume a game with a value of 5 or more.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: 0 in attract, 1 during a one-player game; the reset path requires it non-zero to resume a game.
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware copies it to the display at 0x408D at boot (LDA 407F / STA 408D).
credits.label: Credits

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.
